exchanges.speaker: Pilot
exchanges.text: Hong Kong Radar, Cathay two five one, passing Flight Level one wun zero climbing to Flight Level one six zero.
exchanges.meaning: Check-in while climbing: passing FL110, cleared to FL160.

exchanges.speaker: ATC
exchanges.text: Cathay two five one, Hong Kong Radar, radar contact, turn left heading zero seven zero, vector for sequencing.
exchanges.meaning: ATC establishes radar contact and issues a radar vector: turn left to heading 070 for sequencing.

exchanges.speaker: Pilot
exchanges.text: Turn left heading zero seven zero, vector for sequencing, Cathay two five one.
exchanges.meaning: Pilot reads back the heading instruction and the vector's purpose.

exchanges.speaker: ATC
exchanges.text: Cathay two five one, turn left heading zero two zero, descend to five thousand feet.
exchanges.meaning: ATC vectors the aircraft onto heading 020 with a descent to 5,000 ft.

exchanges.speaker: Pilot
exchanges.text: Hong Kong Radar, Cathay two five one, unable descent to five thousand feet on heading zero two zero due high terrain, minimum vectoring altitude is seven thousand feet.
exchanges.meaning: Pilot exercises the terrain veto: unable the descent due to high terrain, stating the minimum vectoring altitude of 7,000 ft.

exchanges.speaker: ATC
exchanges.text: Cathay two five one, roger, maintain seven thousand feet, maintain heading zero seven zero.
exchanges.meaning: ATC accepts the veto and amends the clearance: maintain 7,000 ft and heading 070.

exchanges.speaker: Pilot
exchanges.text: Maintain seven thousand feet, maintain heading zero seven zero, Cathay two five one.
exchanges.meaning: Pilot reads back the amended altitude and heading.

exchanges.speaker: Pilot
exchanges.text: Fly heading zero niner zero, descending to Flight Level one zero zero, Cathay two five one.
exchanges.meaning: Correct readback form: say 'heading' (never 'track') and always include 'Flight Level'.

vocabulary.definition: A tactical ATC heading instruction that takes the aircraft off its planned route.
Command to turn to a specific magnetic compass heading.
Command to establish and maintain a magnetic heading without wind correction.
ATC states the intent of the vector, e.g. sequencing or spacing.
Vector termination; the pilot resumes the FMC route.
Lowest altitude at which ATC may vector an aircraft while guaranteeing terrain clearance.
The pilot's terrain veto: the pilot-in-command's ultimate responsibility for terrain safety.

quiz.question: When an air traffic controller instructs an aircraft to turn right heading 270, what is the pilot expected to do regarding wind drift?
options: Calculate wind drift and fly ground track 270 degrees
Steer magnetic heading 270 degrees and make no correction for wind drift
quiz.explanation: A vector is an instruction to steer a specific magnetic compass heading. The pilot maintains that heading without applying a drift correction; ATC accounts for wind on radar.

quiz.question: Under ICAO procedures, what action should a pilot take if instructed to descend below the Minimum Safe Altitude (MSA) while on radar vectors in IMC?
options: Comply immediately because ATC has legal radar authority
Descend at a reduced vertical speed
Immediately challenge the clearance, state inability due terrain, and maintain safe altitude
quiz.explanation: The pilot-in-command retains ultimate responsibility for terrain separation. If a clearance conflicts with terrain awareness or safe altitudes, the crew must query ATC immediately and level off.

sections.heading: Core Learning Content -- Radar Vectors & Heading Control
sections.body:
- Turn left / right heading [degrees]: Command to turn to a specific magnetic compass heading.
- Fly heading [degrees]: Command to establish and maintain a magnetic heading without wind correction.
- Vector for [reason]: Stating intent (e.g. sequencing, spacing, traffic avoidance).
- Maintain present heading: Freezing lateral turns.
- Resume own navigation direct [fix]: Vector termination; resuming FMC route.

sections.heading: Spaced Repetition Drill
sections.body:
- Day 13 Review (+1d): Crossing 9,000 ft TA at Hong Kong, call "Standard set, cross-checked" and switch altimeter subscale to 1013.25 hPa.
- Day 7 Review (+7d): Never cross an illuminated red stop-bar even if cleared by ATC.
- Day 1 Review (+14d): Single-digit phonetics: Heading 359 = "TREE FIFE NIN-ER", Altitude 9,000 = "NIN-ER TOU-ZAND".

sections.heading: Fun Aviation Fact
sections.body: The 1974 TWA Flight 514 crash near Washington Dulles led directly to the creation of mapped Minimum Vectoring Altitudes (MVAs) and the global mandate for Ground Proximity Warning Systems (GPWS).
